skill.displayName: Frontend Design Pro — 专业前端设计规范

version.changelog: Initial release: 前端设计质量提升，anti-patterns + 设计命令，参考 impeccable 项目

llm.summary: This is a frontend design guidance skill with no executable code, persistence, credential use, or hidden data access.

dimensions.detail: The skill only instructs the agent on frontend design output and does not request filesystem, network, credential, account, or privileged environment access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact is a single Markdown skill file with no install script, bundled executable, dependency installation, or remote code retrieval.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad UI/design natural-language triggers and says to apply its design rules automatically for design-related requests; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users may want to invoke it only when they want opinionated design guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background workers, scheduled tasks, memory writing, tool wrapping, privilege escalation, or session/profile access was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact consistently describes a frontend/UI design review and polishing skill that guides typography, color, spacing, motion, interaction, and UX writing decisions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want opinionated frontend design defaults and review commands. Expect it to push specific style preferences, such as avoiding Inter/system-ui and applying its design rules during UI work; skip or disable it for projects where those design choices conflict with an existing design system.
llm.findings:
[SQP-3] expected: The skill is written in Chinese, but the artifact does not instruct the agent to force Chinese responses or override a user's language preference; this is not a material security concern.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad Chinese design trigger phrases can activate the skill in ordinary UI-improvement requests, but that behavior is coherent with the stated frontend design purpose and is disclosed in the manifest.
[SQP-1] expected: The automatic application rule for design-related requests is opinionated and somewhat broad, but it is limited to design/code style guidance and does not introduce hidden access, execution, persistence, or data handling.
